tags: why does my dog put their paw on me
script: You're sitting there, minding your own business, and suddenly a paw lands right on your arm, your leg, sometimes your face, like your dog is trying to get your attention the old-fashioned way. And honestly, that's usually exactly what's happening. A paw touch is one of the clearest, most direct ways a dog can physically initiate contact with you, since they don't have hands, that paw is basically standing in for a tap on the shoulder. It often means, I want something, more pets, playtime, dinner, or simply your focus back on them instead of your phone or the TV. Some dogs also learn that pawing gets a reliable reaction, so if you respond every single time, you're quietly reinforcing it as their go-to attention move. It can also show up during play, as a way of initiating, or occasionally as a soft, affectionate gesture, almost like your dog reaching out to touch base with you. It's rarely about dominance or anything negative, it's mostly just your dog's version of saying, hey, I'm right here, notice me. Whether you respond every time or not is really just about what habit you want to build.
